neighbours.label: the word marking what is given in return in an exchange ('in exchange for', 'in return for', 'worth the price of')
fire: I received this novel free from the author in exchange for an honest review.
The farmer let us camp in his field in return for help with the harvest.
The chapter on grammar alone is worth the price of the book.
She agreed to babysit on Friday in exchange for a ride to the airport.
The town gave the company tax breaks in return for new jobs.
He offered to fix her fence if she would lend him the ladder.
Fans got a free poster in exchange for signing up to the newsletter.
The prisoners were released in return for a promise of peace.
quiet: I received this novel from the author last week and read it on the train.
The farmer let us camp in his field for three nights in July.
The chapter on grammar is the longest part of the book.
She agreed to babysit on Friday for most of the evening.
The town gave the company a warm welcome at the opening.
He offered to fix her fence on a sunny afternoon.
Fans got a free poster at the entrance to the concert hall.
The prisoners were released early in the morning on Monday.

notes: card: peaks on ' for' in 'in exchange for'/'in return for', ' of' in 'worth the price of', ' if' in a conditional deal, ' away' in 'giving away'. Near misses keep 'for'/'of' without an exchange.
